meta.title: Example B — Swap branches and multi-asset liquidity (synthetic)
meta.description: A zap contract splits the user's Token X into two swap branches (X→Y in pool XY, X→Z in pool XZ), merges Y and Z into pool YZ to mint LP-YZ for the user, and lets the user stake the LP in a farm. Exiting the LP returns both Y and Z.

boundaries.reason: Reward emission is not modelled in this example.

assumptions.text: All three pools run the same ExamplePair code (constant-product AMM).

notes: Synthetic example data for exercising the viewer. Names, code, addresses and transactions are invented.

unresolved.text: Swap outputs depend on pool reserves at execution time. Only the final LP amount is bounded (minLp); each branch has no own slippage limit.
Farm rewards are not modelled; the stake record is treated as a claim on the staked LP only.

tasks.question: Into which branches is the user's Token X split, and where do they merge?
tasks.answer: Half goes X→Y through pair XY, the rest X→Z through pair XZ; Y and Z merge in pair YZ, which mints LP-YZ to the user.

tasks.question: Which assets does the LP-YZ position give a claim on, and who holds them?
tasks.answer: Pro-rata claims on the Y and Z reserves held by pair YZ. The LP is not counted in addition to those reserves.

tasks.question: Who holds the Token X the user paid in?
tasks.answer: Pairs XY and XZ (their reserves). The user no longer has a claim on that X.

tasks.question: What does exiting the staked position return, and how many steps does it take?
tasks.answer: Two separate calls: unstake (returns LP-YZ), then remove liquidity (returns Y and Z).
